finding.claim: SQL injection via unparameterized ORDER BY: $_GET['sort'] is concatenated into the SQL text passed to PDO::query, allowing attacker-supplied SQL expressions (e.g. boolean/time-based blind extraction via CASE/subqueries).
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) (list.php:6)

trace.note: concatenated into ORDER BY clause of the SQL string

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, cast, quoting, or prepared binding on the path; ?? 'id' default applies only when the parameter is absent. Reachability from an HTTP handler is not shown in this directory (precondition noted); PDO query() on SQLite executes only the first statement, so stacked writes are unlikely, but data read via blind injection remains possible. Not a decoy: list_users_safe uses a closed constant map, but this function does not.

verdict.guard_found: none. list.php:5 takes $_GET['sort'] with only a ?? 'id' default, and list.php:6 concatenates it into the ORDER BY text passed to ->query() with no allowlist, cast, quoting, or binding. The allowlist in list_users_safe (list.php:10-11) is not on this path.
verdict.reason: The source, concatenation, and sink at list.php:5-6 match the candidate exactly and no control is applied, but list_users_sorted is defined at list.php:4 and never called anywhere in this directory, so the attacker-to-sink path depends on a caller that is not present, and I cannot confirm that an unauthenticated HTTP request can reach it.
